doc: The lattice index wraps by & 255 (two's complement for negatives: -1 & 255 = 255): 80 base points with cells in 0..255 and fractions that are multiples of 1/64 (so the float32 coordinates are exact up to +-71000), repeated shifted by multiples of 256 on each axis (both signs, up to 70656), and once shifted into negative cells. Outputs are bit-identical across the three copies of a point (asserted when building the case). Same tolerance as perlin3.f32.random. The permutation input plan<i>.perm is the draw as recorded (256 entries for Perlin3, 1024 for Worley3); the kernel indexes it DOUBLED, concat(perm, perm) (512 or 2048 entries, so p[i + 256] = p[i]): a port that indexes the stored array directly runs off its end (see the .table cases).
